subject: DPA: retention evidence & handover walkthrough for EU onramp
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@aurorahealth.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, tom.berger@aurorahealth.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA evidence request for EU onboarding (Aurora onramp)

Hannah / Laura —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our compliance review before the EU production onramp, legal is asking for a concrete list of the types of evidence and the expected timelines we can provide to show retention and deletion behavior for customer data.

Attached is a spreadsheet that lays out the items we typically ask vendors for (Aurora_Evidence_Ask.xlsx). Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation that customer-requested erasure triggers a verified deletion workflow for primary data and snapshots/backups; whether that includes backups stored for disaster recovery in another region.
- A mapping of where data is stored (region-level) and which artifacts are considered part of the retention window (logs, telemetry, KV cache, snapshots).
- A short description of how you produce a proof-of-erasure certificate and how long it takes.

We'd appreciate a short walkthrough of what Redwood can deliver (documents / timelines / playbooks) and a list of suggested DPA redline language if you think anything in Annex B needs tightening for our regulatory scope. We are trying to finalize the Annex B language by next week (May 9).

Can you confirm whether backups in AZ-west are treated by your onramp process as subject to the same 30-day erase target, or if those are handled under a separate DR retention carveout? Tom (cc'd) will coordinate the technical follow-up.

Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Aurora Health

Attachment: Aurora_Evidence_Ask.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA evidence request for EU onboarding (Aurora onramp)

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. We can do a focused walkthrough and provide a concise evidence packet for the Annex B review. Quick answers up front:
- We support customer-initiated erasure that covers primary stores and ORK (operational key/value caches). Snapshots and DR backups are handled by a controlled workflow — they are not immediately deleted at the point of request to avoid data integrity risks; instead we perform a certified purge on the next maintenance window and provide a certificate.
- Region mapping: we will supply a region-level inventory for the onramp tenants (EU: eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 locations) and label any cross-region replication used for HA.
- Proof-of-erasure: we produce a signed certificate that includes timestamp, affected object IDs, and an audit log excerpt. Typical turnaround is 24–72 hours depending on whether any legal holds are active.

We have a playbook draft (redwood_onramp_erase_playbook_v2.docx) and a short proof matrix PDF I can attach. Marcus, can you add the exact snapshot lifecycle and the expected purge schedule for cross-region backups so we can answer the AZ-west question concretely?

Next step: propose a 45-minute walkthrough on Fri May 3 at 10am BST / 2am PT — if that works for you we will share the packet in advance.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Compliance (onramp)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_onramp_erase_playbook_v2.docx (draft playbook)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA evidence request for EU onboarding (Aurora onramp)

Hannah / Emma / Tom —

Technical detail to supplement Hannah's note:
- Snapshots/backups: we maintain incremental snapshots with a 14-day hot retention window for quick restores and a cold snapshot archival tier retained up to 90 days by default for onramp customers. For Aurora's EU tenant we can change the cold retention floor to 30 days via a config flag attached to the customer tenant, and enable the certified purge flow on request.
- Cross-region DR (AZ-west): our replication pipeline creates a logical copy in the DR region. Those copies are bound to the same deletion process but require a DR purge run during the next maintenance cycle. Practically, that means customer-initiated erasure + no legal hold => cross-region copies are purged in the next 24–72 hour DR maintenance window. If Aurora requires a hard 30-day SLA across all copies, we can contractually commit and operationalize it as a schedule with a documented runbook.
- Logs & telemetry: ephemeral logs (level=debug/traces) are rotated daily and kept for 7 days; security/audit logs are retained 90 days by default and can be exported on demand. We will include an audit log slice with each proof-of-erasure.
- Proof artifact: redwood produces a zipped evidence bundle that includes (a) audit log excerpt, (b) deletion job ids, (c) signed certificate with SHA256 of deleted object ids, (d) operator verification entry. We can encrypt the package with Aurora's public key if needed.

I'll attach a short matrix that maps artifacts -> retention -> purge cadence. Laura / Karthik: please review the proposed language below for Annex B (very high level) and flag any legal/operational items:

Proposed snippet for Annex B (operational): "Upon receipt of a verified erasure request, Redwood will: (i) mark the customer's primary objects for deletion immediately; (ii) schedule any snapshot / backup purges within the next 72 hours unless subject to an active lawful hold; (iii) provide a signed proof-of-erasure certificate within 72 hours of completion of purge operations."

Noting this is operationally accurate for the onramp flow; happy to shorten SLA windows if Aurora needs a 24–48 hour guarantee and to call that out as a contract amendment.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_AnnexB_proof_matrix.pdf (artifact matrix)
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@aurorahealth.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: tom.berger@aurorahealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA evidence request for EU onboarding (Aurora onramp)

Hannah / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick and detailed responses, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from legal:
1) Can you confirm which specific object identifiers are included in the "deleted object ids" list in the proof certificate (e.g., dataset ids, tenant ids, snapshot ids)? We need a mapping to our internal patient datasets so we can reconcile.
2) For the Annex B snippet, legal prefers a single SLA number where possible. They asked whether Redwood can make the Annex B operational language read: "Redwood will complete certified purge of all customer-controlled artifacts (primary objects, snapshots, and cross-region backups) within 72 hours of receipt of a verified erasure request unless an active lawful hold is in place." If you can accept this as written, please confirm.
3) If Redwood can produce the encrypted evidence bundle to our key, that will satisfy our evidence chain requirements — please note this in the packet.

We will take the walkthrough tomorrow but would like to see the redline suggestion for Annex B before the meeting if possible. If you're able to accept the 72-hour single-SLA language above, that simplifies our redline and speeds the onramp.

Thanks —
Emma
